title: Outlook mobile: Purview DLP policy tips for iOS and Android (Worldwide)
summary: Hold: the briefing describes override justification options as noncustomizable without limiting that statement to the default dialog, although Microsoft documents customizable options on mobile. Its medium cost rating also relies on desktop licensing that the briefing itself says is not confirmed for mobile. The roadmap facts, administrator-enabled default and documented commands check out.

claims.claim: The mobile reference requires necessary licenses and configuration for the oversharing dialog but names no licenses.

claims.claim: Where a rule allows an override, the dialog uses a noncustomizable set of justification options.

Customized oversharing dialog

You can choose to tailor your oversharing dialog with a customized title, body, and dynamic variables like %%MatchedRecipientsList%%, and justification options.

The default-dialog qualification is stated at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/dlp-outlook-mobile-policy-tip-ref.

claims.claim: When auditing is enabled, Cloud Policy configuration and setting changes are tracked and searchable through Purview or PowerShell.
claims.quote: When auditing is enabled, events such as the creation, deletion, modification of policy configurations, changes to configured policy settings, and adjustments to priority order are tracked. You can use the portal or PowerShell to search the audit log for such changes.

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview portal > Data loss prevention > Policies is the documented starting page for configuring a DLP rule's popup dialog.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Data loss prevention > Policies ... Select Policy tips > Show the policy tip as a dialog for the end user before send (available for Exchange workload only).
claims.fix: Retain the accurate policy-list path, but replace its note's first sentence with: "Path stops at the policy list; the documented rule option is Policy tips > Show the policy tip as a dialog for the end user before send (available for Exchange workload only), with User notifications set to On." See https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/dlp-osp-get-started.

claims.claim: Set-DlpComplianceRule -Identity <rule name> -NotifyPolicyTipDisplayOption Dialog sets a popup policy tip for Exchange in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: This cmdlet is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell. ... The Identity parameter specifies the DLP rule that you want to modify. ... -NotifyPolicyTipDisplayOption ... Dialog: Displays policy tip at the top of the mail and as a popup dialog. (exchange only)

claims.where: front matter: cost; rationale: cost; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Medium is the supported cost rating for this mobile feature because advanced Outlook for Microsoft 365 tips require E5-tier licenses.
claims.quote: cost: "medium" ... Whether the Outlook for Microsoft 365 list applies unchanged to mobile is not stated on that page. ... The indirect cost is administrator time to pilot and user communication.
claims.fix: Set cost to "low". Replace the cost rationale with: "Low. The known cost is administrator time to pilot and communicate the change; the mobile page does not name the required licences, and it does not state whether the advanced Outlook for Microsoft 365 licence list applies unchanged to mobile." Keep the qualified desktop license list in Cost and licensing. The schema requires low when licensing is unresolved and the known cost is administrator time.
